en: I bow to Shambhu, husband of Uma, teacher of the gods; I bow to the cause of the world. I bow to him who wears serpents as ornaments and holds a deer; I bow to the lord of all creatures. I bow to him whose eyes are the sun, moon and fire; I bow to the one dear to Mukunda. I bow to the refuge of devotees, the giver of boons; I bow to Shiva, Shankara.

first: ततस्स प्रयतो भूत्वा मम तात युधिष्ठिर ।
en: Vasudeva said: My dear Yudhishthira, then that Brahmin sage, having made himself pure and with joined palms, began to recite the collection of names from the beginning.
Upamanyu said: I will praise the one who is worthy of praise and famous in all the worlds, using names spoken by Brahma and by the sages, which come from the Vedas and their branches.
These names were set out by great beings; they are true and proven and bring every aim to success. They were gathered with devotion by the sage Tandi, whose mind was shaped by the Veda.
They were spoken just so by good and famous sages who saw the truth. This hymn is the best and foremost, leads to heaven, and is good and auspicious for all beings.
These true names, spoken by Brahma, brought down from the world of Brahma and heard everywhere in the world, are the highest, eternal Brahman.
Best of the Yadus, I will tell them; listen to me with full attention. Choose this God Bhava, the Supreme Lord, as your own, being his devotee.
So I will let you hear that which is the eternal Brahman. No one can describe Sharva fully and in detail,
even with all their powers and even over hundreds of years. Even the gods cannot reach his beginning, middle or end.
Madhava, who could describe all his qualities completely? But I will tell, in brief words and syllables, of the great God,
and of his deeds, as far as I am able, by the grace of that wise one. Without first gaining his permission, the Lord cannot be praised.

first: यदा तेनाभ्यनुज्ञातस्स्तुतो वै स तदा मया ।
en: When he had given me permission, then I praised him. I will tell a small part of the names of that great one, who has no beginning or end and is the source of the world,
whose origin is not seen, who gives boons, who is worthy to be chosen, who has all forms and is wise.

first: शृणु नाम्नां चयं कृष्ण यदुक्तं पद्मयोनिना ।
en: Krishna, hear this collection of names spoken by the lotus-born Brahma, the great-grandfather, who spoke ten thousand names.
Churning those ten thousand names in the mind, this was drawn out, as butter is drawn from curd, as gold is the best of a mountain, as honey is the best of flowers,
as cream is the best of butter: so this essence was drawn out. It removes all sins and contains the four Vedas.
It should be learned with effort and kept in mind with a controlled self. It is auspicious, nourishing, destroys evil spirits, and is greatly purifying.
It should be given to a devotee who has faith and who believes, not to one without faith, a non-believer, or one who has not controlled himself.
Krishna, whoever finds fault with the God, the Lord who is the cause of all, goes to hell together with his ancestors and his children.
This is meditation, this is yoga, this is the highest thing to meditate on. This is to be repeated, this is knowledge, this is the highest secret.

first: यं ज्ञात्वा ह्यन्तकालेऽपि गच्छेत परमां गतिम् ।
en: Knowing this, a person reaches the highest goal even at the time of death. It is holy, auspicious, pure, good and the best of all.
Long ago Brahma, grandfather of all the worlds, composed this and set it as the king of all divine hymns.
Since then this hymn to the great Lord has been known in the world as the King of Hymns, worshipped by the immortals.
This King of Hymns was brought down from the world of Brahma to heaven. Because Tandi received it long ago, it became known as the hymn made by Tandi.
Tandi brought it down from heaven to this earth. It is the most auspicious of all auspicious things and destroys all sins.
Mighty-armed one, I will tell you this best of hymns about him who is the Brahman of all Brahmans and the highest of all that is high,
the light of all lights, the austerity of all austerities, the calmest of the calm, the brilliance of all brilliance,

first: दान्तानामपि यो दान्तो धीमतामपि या च धीः ।
en: the most self-controlled of the self-controlled, the wisdom of the wise, the God of the gods and the seer among seers,
the sacrifice of sacrifices, the most auspicious of the auspicious, the Rudra of the Rudras and the radiance of the mighty,

first: योगिनामपि यो योगी कारणानां च कारणम् ।
en: the yogi of yogis and the cause of causes, from whom the worlds come into being and into whom they go again.
Hear from me the thousand and eight names of Hara, of boundless brilliance, who is the self of all beings and is everything.

Tiger among men, hearing them you will gain all your wishes. He is steady (Sthira), firm as a pillar (Sthanu), the master (Prabhu), the terrible (Bhima), the foremost (Pravara), the giver of boons (Varada) and the best (Vara).

He is the self of all (Sarvatma), known to all (Sarvavikhyata), everything (Sarva), the maker of all (Sarvakara), existence (Bhava), with matted hair (Jati), wearing skins (Charmi), with a tuft of hair (Shikhandi), whose body is everything (Sarvanga) and the one who brings all into being (Sarvabhavana).

He is the remover (Hara), deer-eyed (Harinaksha), the one who takes away all beings (Sarvabhutahara), the master (Prabhu), the path of action (Pravritti) and the path of withdrawal (Nivritti), the disciplined (Niyata), eternal (Shashvata) and fixed (Dhruva).

He lives in the cremation ground (Shmashanavasi), is the Blessed Lord (Bhagavan), moves in the sky (Khachara), moves on the earth (Gochara), the tormentor of the wicked (Ardana), worthy of salutation (Abhivadya), of great deeds (Mahakarma), the ascetic (Tapasvi) and the creator of beings (Bhutabhavana).

He dresses like a madman (Unmattavesha), is hidden (Prachchhanna), the lord of creatures of all worlds (Sarvalokaprajapati), of great form (Maharupa), of great body (Mahakaya), in the form of a bull (Vrisharupa) and of great fame (Mahayasha).

He is the great soul (Mahatma), the self of all beings (Sarvabhutatma), with all forms (Vishvarupa), with a great jaw (Mahahanu), guardian of the world (Lokapala), the hidden self (Antarhitatma), grace itself (Prasada) and blue and red (Nilalohita).

He is the pure (Pavitra), the great (Mahan), the rule (Niyama), the one who keeps rules (Niyamashrita), the doer of all deeds (Sarvakarma), self-born (Svayambhuta), the beginning (Adi), the maker of the beginning (Adikara) and the treasure (Nidhi).

He is thousand-eyed (Sahasraksha), large-eyed (Vishalaksha), the moon (Soma), the one who guides the stars (Nakshatrasadhaka), the moon (Chandra), the sun (Surya), Saturn (Shani), Ketu, the planet (Graha), the lord of planets (Grahapati) and the best (Vara).

He is the beginning (Adi) and the end (Anta), dissolution (Laya), the doer (Karta), the one who shot the arrow at the deer (Mrigabanarpana), sinless (Anagha), of great austerity (Mahatapa), of fierce austerity (Ghoratapa), never downcast (Adina) and the helper of the downcast (Dinasadhaka).

He makes the year (Samvatsarakara), is the sacred mantra (Mantra), the measure of truth (Pramana), the highest austerity (Paramam Tapa), the yogi (Yogi), the one to be joined in yoga (Yojya), the great seed (Mahabija), of great seed (Mahareta) and of great strength (Mahabala).

His seed is golden (Suvarnareta); he is all-knowing (Sarvajna), the good seed (Subija), the bearer of seeds (Bijavahana), ten-armed (Dashabahu), unblinking (Animisha), blue-throated (Nilakantha) and husband of Uma (Umapati).

He has all forms (Vishvarupa), is best by himself (Svayamshreshtha), strong and heroic (Balavira), strength (Bala), the host (Gana), the maker of hosts (Ganakarta), lord of hosts (Ganapati), clothed by the directions (Digvasa) and desire (Kama).

He knows the mantras (Mantravit), is the highest mantra (Paramo Mantra), the maker of all states (Sarvabhavakara), the remover (Hara), holder of the water pot (Kamandaludhara), the archer (Dhanvi), arrow in hand (Banahasta) and the bearer of a skull (Kapalavan).

first: अशनी शतघ्नी खड्गी पट्टिशी चायुधी महान् ।
en: He bears the thunderbolt (Ashani), the hundred-killer weapon (Shataghni), the sword (Khadgi) and the spear (Pattishi); he is armed (Ayudhi), great (Mahan), holds the sacrificial ladle (Sruvahasta), is handsome (Surupa), brilliance (Teja), maker of brilliance (Tejaskara) and the treasure (Nidhi).
He wears a turban (Ushnishi), has a fine face (Suvaktra), is lofty (Udagra), humble (Vinata), tall (Dirgha), with tawny hair (Harikesha), the good holy place (Sutirtha) and dark (Krishna).

He takes the form of a jackal (Srigalarupa), has his aims fulfilled (Siddhartha), is shaven (Munda), the doer of all good (Sarvashubhankara), unborn (Aja), of many forms (Bahurupa), the bearer of the Ganga (Gangadhari) and the one with braided hair (Kapardi).

He is perfectly chaste (Urdhvareta), with the linga raised (Urdhvalinga), lying upward (Urdhvashayi), whose place is the sky (Nabhahsthala), with three locks of hair (Trijata), dressed in bark (Chiravasa), Rudra, the army chief (Senapati) and all-pervading (Vibhu).

He moves by night (Naktanchara) and by day (Ahashchara), has fierce anger (Tigmamanyu), is very radiant (Suvarchasa), the slayer of the elephant demon (Gajaha), slayer of demons (Daityaha), time (Kala), upholder of the world (Lokadhata) and a mine of virtues (Gunakara).

He takes the form of a lion and a tiger (Simhashardularupa), is clothed in a tiger skin (Vyaghracharmambaravrita), the yogi of time (Kalayogi), the great lord (Mahanatha), the fulfiller of all desires (Sarvakama) and the meeting of four roads (Chatushpatha).

He moves at night (Nishachara), is king of the departed spirits (Pretaraja), moves among ghosts (Bhutachari), the Great Lord (Maheshvara), the many beings (Bahubhuta), bearer of many (Bahudhara), Rahu (Svarbhanu), the limitless (Amita) and the goal (Gati).

He loves dance (Nrityapriya), dances always (Nityanarta), is the dancer (Nartaka), ever eager (Sadalalasa), of very fierce austerity (Mahaghoratapa), brave (Shura), eternal (Nitya), free of striving (Aniha) and without a home (Niralaya).

He has a thousand hands (Sahasrahasta), is victory (Vijaya), resolve (Vyavasaya), never tired (Atandrita), unforgiving of evil (Amarshana), of stern nature (Amarshanatma), the destroyer of the sacrifice (Yajnaha) and the destroyer of Kama (Kamanashaka).

He wrecked Daksha's sacrifice (Dakshayagapahari), is very patient (Susaha), the middle (Madhyama), the taker of brilliance (Tejopahari), slayer of the demon Bala (Balaha), joyful (Mudita), the aim (Artha), unconquered (Ajita) and the best (Vara).

He has a deep voice (Gambhiraghosha), is deep (Gambhira), has a deep and strong mount (Gambhirabalavahana), takes the form of the banyan (Nyagrodharupa), rests on a banyan leaf (Nyagrodhavrikshakarnasthiti) and is all-pervading (Vibhu).

He has very sharp teeth (Sutikshnadashana), a great body (Mahakaya), a great mouth (Mahanana); he is the one whose army is everywhere (Vishvaksena), the one to whom Hari offers sacrifice (Hariyajna) and the one whose mount crushes foes in battle (Samyugapidavahana).

He has fierce heat (Tikshnatapa), has tawny horses (Haryashva), is the helper (Sahaya), knows the right time for action (Karmakalavit), is pleased by Vishnu (Vishnuprasadita), the sacrifice (Yajna), the ocean (Samudra) and the mare-faced fire under the sea (Badabamukha).

He is the friend of fire (Hutashanasahaya), of peaceful nature (Prashantatma), fire itself (Hutashana), of fierce brilliance (Ugrateja), of great brilliance (Mahateja), the warrior (Janya) and the one who knows the time of victory (Vijayakalavit).

He is the path of the stars (Jyotishamayana), success (Siddhi), the form of all (Sarvavigraha), with a crest (Shikhi), shaven (Mundi), with matted hair (Jati), flaming (Jvali), born in forms (Murtija), dwelling in the head (Murdhaga) and strong (Bali).

He is devoted to Vishnu (Vaishnava), swift (Prajavi), the one who claps the rhythm (Tali), playful (Kheli), the one who holds back death (Kalakatankata), whose mind knows the forms of the stars (Nakshatravigrahamati), whose mind knows the qualities (Gunabuddhi), dissolution (Laya) and the unmoving (Agama). He is the lord of creatures (Prajapati), with arms everywhere (Vishvabahu), the one who divides (Vibhaga), facing all sides (Sarvatomukha), the releaser (Vimochana), the one who gives a good death (Sumarana) and the source of the golden armour (Hiranyakavachodbhava).

He is born of the clouds (Meghaja), moves with strength (Balachari), moves on the earth (Mahichari), is praised (Stuta), delights in all musical instruments (Sarvaturyavinodi) and accepts all music (Sarvavadyaparigraha).

He takes the form of a serpent (Vyalarupa), lives in caves (Guhavasi), wears the planets as a garland (Grahamali), knows the waves (Tarangavit), is the god (Tridasha), sees all time (Kaladrik) and frees from all bonds of action (Karmasarvabandhavimochana).

He binds the demon kings (Asurendranam Bandhana), destroys enemies in battle (Yudhi Shatruvinashana), is the grace of Sankhya (Sankhyaprasada), Durvasa, and is served by all the good (Sarvasadhunishevita).

He makes the enemy flee (Praskandana), knows how to share out (Vibhagajna), is matchless (Atulya), knows each one's share in the sacrifice (Yajnabhagavit), dwells in all (Sarvavasa), moves in all (Sarvachari), is Durvasa, Indra (Vasava) and immortal (Amara).

He is golden (Haima), the maker of gold (Hemakara), the sacrifice (Yajna), the bearer of all (Sarvadhari), the best of supporters (Dharottama), red-eyed (Lohitaksha), large-eyed (Mahaksha), with victorious eyes (Vijayaksha) and skilful (Visharada).

He gathers in (Sangraha), restrains (Nigraha), is the doer (Karta), dressed in snakes and bark (Sarpachiranivasana), the chief (Mukhya), not the chief (Amukhya), the body (Deha), the drum Kahali, and the giver of all desires (Sarvakamada).

He is gracious at all times (Sarvakalaprasada), very strong (Subala), bears the form of strength (Balarupabhrit), gives all desires (Sarvakamaprada), gives everything (Sarvada) and faces every side (Sarvatomukha).

He is formless like the sky (Akashanirvirupa), the one who falls on foes (Nipata), free of control (Avasha), the bird in the sky (Khaga), of fierce form (Raudrarupa), the ray (Amshu), the sun (Aditya), with many rays (Bahurashmi) and very radiant (Suvarchasi).

He has the speed of the Vasus (Vasuvega), great speed (Mahavega), the speed of the mind (Manovega), moves at night (Nishachara), dwells in all (Sarvavasi), dwells with fortune (Shriyavasi), is the teacher (Upadeshakara) and the one who does nothing (Akara).

He is the sage (Muni), the Self (Atma), beyond sight (Niraloka), the one who breaks (Sambhagna), the giver of thousands (Sahasrada), the bird (Pakshi), in the form of the plaksha tree (Plaksharupa), very bright (Atidipta) and lord of people (Vishampati).

He is madness (Unmada), the intoxicating one (Madana), desire (Kama), the holy fig tree (Ashvattha), the giver of wealth (Arthakara), fame (Yasha), Vamadeva, the lovely (Vama), facing east, south and north (Pragdakshina Udanmukha).

He is the perfect yogi (Siddhayogi), the great sage (Maharshi), with aims fulfilled (Siddhartha), the bringer of perfection (Siddhasadhaka), the beggar monk (Bhikshu), in the form of a beggar (Bhikshurupa), Vipaga, gentle (Mridu) and undying (Avyaya).

He is the great general (Mahasena), Vishakha, the sixtieth part (Shashtibhaga), lord of cows (Gavampati), thunderbolt in hand (Vajrahasta), the support (Vishkambhi) and the one who halts armies (Chamustambhana).

He is the one who keeps the right conduct (Vrittavrittakara), the palm tree (Tala), sweet (Madhu), with honey-coloured eyes (Madhukalochana), the lord of speech (Vachaspatya), the giver of food (Vajasana) and the one always worshipped by those who seek shelter (Nityam Ashritapujita).

He is the celibate student (Brahmachari), moves through the world (Lokachari), moves everywhere (Sarvachari), knows how to reason (Vicharavit), the ruler (Ishana), the Lord (Ishvara), time (Kala), moves at night (Nishachari) and holds the bow Pinaka (Pinakabhrit).

He is present in every cause (Nimittastha), the cause itself (Nimitta), Nandi, the maker of joy (Nandikara), Hari, the lord of Nandi (Nandishvara), Nandi, the delight (Nandana) and the one who increases joy (Nandivardhana).

first: भगहारी निहन्ता च कालो ब्रह्मा पितामहः ।
en: He took away the fortune of Bhaga (Bhagahari), is the slayer (Nihanta), time (Kala), Brahma, the grandfather (Pitamaha), four-faced (Chaturmukha), the great linga (Mahalinga) and the lovely linga (Charulinga).

He is the overseer of the linga (Lingadhyaksha), of the gods (Suradhyaksha), of yoga (Yogadhyaksha), the bringer of disease to the wicked (Rugavaha), the overseer of seeds (Bijadhyaksha), the maker of seeds (Bijakarta), the one who follows the inner self (Adhyatmanugata) and strength (Bala).

He is history (Itihasa), the ritual texts (Sakalpa), Gautama, the moon (Nishakara), pretence (Dambha), free of pretence (Adambha), Vaidambha, the one who can be won over (Vashya), the one who wins others over (Vashakara) and the age of strife (Kali).

He is the maker of the world (Lokakarta), the lord of creatures (Pashupati), the great maker (Mahakarta), the one who needs no medicine (Anaushadha), the imperishable (Akshara), the highest Brahman (Paramam Brahma), the strong (Balavan) and the able (Shakta).

He is right policy (Niti) and its absence (Aniti), of pure nature (Shuddhatma), pure (Shuddha), honoured (Manya), coming and going (Gatagata), very gracious (Bahuprasada), the giver of good dreams (Susvapna), the mirror (Darpana) and the conqueror of foes (Amitrajit).

He is the maker of the Vedas (Vedakara), the maker of mantras (Mantrakara), the wise (Vidvan), the crusher in battle (Samaramardana), the one who dwells in great clouds (Mahameghanivasi), the very terrible (Mahaghora) and the one who brings others under control (Vashikara).

He is the flame of fire (Agnijvala), the great flame (Mahajvala), very smoky (Atidhumra), the one offered into fire (Huta), the offering (Havi), the bull (Vrishabha), the giver of peace (Shankara), the eternal (Nitya), the radiant (Varchasvi) and the one whose banner is smoke (Dhumaketana).

He is blue (Nila), Angalubdha, the beautiful (Shobhana), unhindered (Niravagraha), the giver of welfare (Svastida), the share of welfare (Svastibhaga), the one who takes a share (Bhagi), the one who gives shares (Bhagakara) and the light (Laghu).

He is the lap that holds all (Utsanga), the great-limbed (Mahanga), the final refuge of the great womb (Mahagarbhaparayana), dark in colour (Krishnavarna), golden (Suvarna) and the senses of all embodied beings (Indriyam Sarvadehinam).

He has great feet (Mahapada), great hands (Mahahasta), a great body (Mahakaya), great fame (Mahayasha), a great head (Mahamurdha), great measure (Mahamatra), great eyes (Mahanetra) and is the home of night (Nishalaya).

He is the great ender (Mahantaka), with great ears (Mahakarna), great lips (Mahoshtha), a great jaw (Mahahanu), a great nose (Mahanasa), a great conch-like neck (Mahakambu), a great neck (Mahagriva) and the one who lives in the cremation ground (Shmashanabhak).

He has a great chest (Mahavaksha), a broad breast (Mahoraska), is the inner Self (Antaratma), the home of deer (Mrigalaya), the one who hangs down (Lambana), with hanging lips (Lambitoshtha), of great magic power (Mahamaya) and the ocean (Payonidhi).

He has great teeth (Mahadanta), great tusks (Mahadamshtra), a great tongue (Mahajihva), a great mouth (Mahamukha), great nails (Mahanakha), great body hair (Maharoma), great hair (Mahakesha) and great matted locks (Mahajata).

He is gracious (Prasanna), grace itself (Prasada), trust (Pratyaya), the one whose means is the mountain (Girisadhana), loving (Snehana), free of attachment (Asnehana), unconquered (Ajita) and the great sage (Mahamuni).

He is shaped like a tree (Vrikshakara), has a tree on his banner (Vrikshaketu), is fire (Anala), the one carried by the wind (Vayuvahana), Gandali, the one whose home is Mount Meru (Merudhama) and the overlord of the gods (Devadhipati).

His head is the Atharva Veda (Atharvashirsha), his mouth the Sama Veda (Samasya), his countless eyes the thousand verses of the Rig Veda (Riksahasramitekshana), his feet and arms the Yajur Veda (Yajuhpadabhuja); he is hidden (Guhya), manifest (Prakasha) and moving (Jangama).

His purpose never fails (Amoghartha); he is grace (Prasada), the one to be approached (Abhigamya), of pleasing look (Sudarshana), the helper (Upakara), the beloved (Priya), everything (Sarva), golden (Kanaka) and gold-coloured (Kanchanachhavi).

He is the navel (Nabhi), the maker of joy (Nandikara), being (Bhava), the builder in the lotus (Pushkarasthapati), the steady (Sthira), the twelfth (Dvadasha), the one who frightens (Trasana), the first (Adya), the sacrifice (Yajna) and the one joined to the sacrifice (Yajnasamahita).

He is the night (Naktam), Kali, time (Kala), the makara (Makara), worshipped by Time (Kalapujita), with his hosts (Sagana), maker of hosts (Ganakara) and the charioteer whose mount is the spirits (Bhutavahanasarathi).

He lies on ashes (Bhasmashaya), guards ashes (Bhasmagopta), has become ashes (Bhasmabhuta), is the tree (Taru), the host (Gana), the guardian of the world (Lokapala), the world (Loka), the great soul (Mahatma) and worshipped by all (Sarvapujita).

He is white (Shukla), endowed with three kinds of purity (Trishuklasampanna), pure (Shuchi), served by spirits (Bhutanishevita), established in the orders of life (Ashramastha), present in the rites (Kriyavastha), the mind behind the making of the universe (Vishvakarmamati) and the best (Vara).

He has wide branches (Vishalashakha), copper-red lips (Tamroshtha), is a net of waters (Ambujala), very steady (Sunishchala), tawny (Kapila), brownish (Kapisha), white (Shukla), life (Ayu), the higher (Para) and the lower (Apara).

He is the Gandharva, Aditi, Tarkshya (Garuda), easy to know (Suvijneya), of fine speech (Susharada), armed with the axe (Parashvadhayudha), the God (Deva), the one who follows his devotees (Anukari) and the good kinsman (Subandhava).

He plays the gourd-lute (Tumbavina), has great anger (Mahakrodha), is perfectly chaste (Urdhvareta), lies in the waters (Jaleshaya), fierce (Ugra), the one who brings under control (Vashankara), the bamboo (Vamsha), the sound of the flute (Vamshanada) and blameless (Anindita).

His form is in every limb (Sarvangarupa); he is the master of magic (Mayavi), the good friend (Suhrida), wind (Anila), fire (Anala), the bond (Bandhana), the maker of bonds (Bandhakarta) and the one who frees from strong bonds (Subandhanavimochana).

He is the foe of Daksha's sacrifice (Yajnari), the foe of Kama (Kamari), with great tusks (Mahadamshtra), with great weapons (Mahayudha), praised in many ways (Bahudha Anindita), everything (Sarva), the giver of peace (Shankara) and the one with the moon on his head (Chandrashekhara).

He is lord of the immortals (Amaresha), the great God (Mahadeva), the god of all (Vishvadeva), slayer of the gods' enemies (Surariha), the serpent of the deep (Ahirbudhnya), like the wind (Anilabha), the wise (Chekitana) and Hari.
He is Ajaikapat, the bearer of skulls (Kapali), Trishanku, the unconquered (Ajita), the auspicious (Shiva), Dhanvantari, the comet (Dhumaketu), Skanda and Vaishravana (Kubera).

first: धाता शक्रश्च विष्णुश्च मित्रस्त्वष्टा ध्रुवो धरः ।
en: He is Dhata, Indra (Shakra), Vishnu, Mitra, Tvashta, the pole star (Dhruva), the bearer (Dhara), power (Prabhava), the all-pervading (Sarvaga), the wind (Vayu), Aryaman, Savita and the sun (Ravi).

He is Ushangu, the arranger (Vidhata), Mandhata, the creator of beings (Bhutabhavana), the all-pervading (Vibhu), the maker of the classes (Varnavibhavi) and the bringer of all desires and good qualities (Sarvakamagunavaha).
He is lotus-navelled (Padmanabha), the great womb (Mahagarbha), moon-faced (Chandravaktra), wind (Anila), fire (Anala), strong (Balavan), calm (Upashanta), the ancient (Purana) and Punyachanchuri.

He made the Kurus (Kurukarta), dwells among the Kurus (Kuruvasi), has become the Kurus (Kurubhuta), is the herb of virtues (Gunaushadha), the resting place of all (Sarvashaya), the one who moves on darbha grass (Darbhachari) and lord of all living creatures (Sarvesham Praninam Pati).

He is the God of gods (Devadeva), the one free from attachment to pleasure (Sukhasakta), what is and what is not (Sadasat), the knower of all jewels (Sarvaratnavit), the dweller on Mount Kailasa (Kailasagirivasi) and the one who takes shelter in the Himalaya (Himavadgirisamshraya).

He carries away the banks (Kulahari), builds the banks (Kulakarta), has much learning (Bahuvidya), gives much (Bahuda), is the merchant (Vanija), the carpenter (Vardhaki), the tree (Vriksha), the bakula tree (Vakula) and the one covered with sandal (Chandanachhada).

He has a strong neck (Saragriva), great collarbones (Mahajatru), is steady (Alola), the great medicine (Mahaushadha), the one who fulfils aims (Siddharthakari), whose aims are fulfilled (Siddhartha) and the one beyond metre and grammar (Chhandovyakaranottara).

He has a lion's roar (Simhanada), a lion's teeth (Simhadamshtra), moves like a lion (Simhaga), rides a lion (Simhavahana), is the soul of power (Prabhavatma), the time of the world (Jagatkala), time (Kala), the one who does good to the world (Lokahita) and the saviour (Tara).

He is Saranga, with nine wheels on his body (Navachakranga), wearing a garland of banners (Ketumali), the one who makes all exist (Sabhavana), the home of beings (Bhutalaya), lord of beings (Bhutapati), day and night (Ahoratra) and blameless (Anindita).

He makes all beings grow (Vardhita), is the home of all beings (Sarvabhutanam Nilaya), all-pervading (Vibhu), existence (Bhava), never fruitless (Amogha), self-controlled (Samyata), the horse (Ashva), the food (Bhojana) and the one who holds up life (Pranadharana).

He is steadfast (Dhritiman), intelligent (Matiman), skilful (Daksha), honoured (Satkrita), lord of the ages (Yugadhipa), the cowherd (Gopali), lord of cows (Gopati), the village (Grama), the one who wears a cow-hide (Gocharmavasana) and Hari.

He has golden arms (Hiranyabahu), guards the caves (Guhapala), is the one who leads in (Praveshaka), the one whose enemies are the passions (Prakrishtari), of great joy (Mahaharsha), the conqueror of desire (Jitakama) and the conqueror of the senses (Jitendriya).

He is the musical note Gandhara, finely dressed (Suvasa), devoted to austerity (Tapassakta), delight (Rati), the man (Nara), the one of great songs (Mahagita) and great dances (Mahanritya), served by hosts of Apsaras (Apsarogana-sevita).

He has a great banner (Mahaketu), is the great mountain (Mahadhatu), moves over many peaks (Naikasanuchara), moves (Chala), is to be made known (Avedaniya), the one who enters into all (Avesha) and the bringer of the joy of all fragrances (Sarvagandhasukhavaha).

He is the gateway (Torana), the one who carries across (Tarana), the wind (Vata), the moving lord of the boundary (Paridhipatikhechara), union (Samyoga), growth (Vardhana), the old (Vriddha), the very old (Ativriddha) and rich in virtues (Gunadhika).

He is the eternal Self (Nitya Atma), the helper (Sahaya), lord of gods and demons (Devasurapati), the Lord (Pati), the joined (Yukta), with ready arms (Yuktabahu), the God (Deva) and the one of fine festivals in heaven (Divi Suparvana).

He is Ashadha, Sushadha, the fixed (Dhruva), the deer (Harina), the remover (Hara), the body of those who return again (Vapuravartamana), the best of the Vasus (Vasushreshtha) and the great path (Mahapatha).

He cut off Brahma's head (Shirohari), is reflection (Vimarsha), marked with every auspicious sign (Sarvalakshanalakshita), the axle (Aksha), joined to the chariot (Rathayogi), the yogi of all (Sarvayogi) and of great strength (Mahabala).

He is the sacred tradition (Samamnaya) and what lies beyond it (Asamamnaya), the god of holy places (Tirthadeva), the great chariot-warrior (Maharatha), lifeless (Nirjiva), life-giving (Jivana), the mantra (Mantra), of auspicious eyes (Shubhaksha) and very harsh to the wicked (Bahukarkasha).

He is rich in jewels (Ratnaprabhuta), red-limbed (Raktanga), the one who drinks the great ocean (Maharnavanipanavit), the root (Mula), the vast (Vishala), immortal (Amrita), both manifest and unmanifest (Vyaktavyakta) and a treasure of austerity (Taponidhi).

He is the ascent (Arohana) and the one who has climbed above (Adhiroha), keeps good conduct (Shiladhari), is of great fame (Mahayasha), the plan of the army (Senakalpa), the great age (Mahakalpa), yoga (Yoga), the maker of yoga (Yogakara) and Hari.

He takes the form of the ages (Yugarupa), is of great form (Maharupa), the slayer of the great serpent (Mahanagahana), death (Vadha), the giver of just shares (Nyayanirvapana), the foot (Pada), the learned (Pandita) and like a mountain (Achalopama).

He wears many garlands (Bahumala) and great garlands (Mahamala), is the moon (Shashi), with lovely tawny eyes (Harisulochana), the expanse (Vistara), salt (Lavana), the well (Kupa), present in three ages (Triyuga) and the one whose rising bears fruit (Saphalodaya).

He is three-eyed (Trilochana), Vishannanga, with jewels pierced in his ears (Manividdha), the bearer of matted hair (Jatadhara), the dot (Bindu), the final breath sound (Visarga), the fair-faced (Sumukha), the arrow (Shara), all weapons (Sarvayudha) and the patient (Saha).

He is the one to whom all is offered (Nivedana), born of joy (Sukhajata), the fragrant one (Sugandhara), with a great bow (Mahadhanu), the guardian of fragrance (Gandhapali), the Blessed Lord (Bhagavan) and the rise of all actions (Utthana Sarvakarmanam).

He is the churning rod (Manthana), the abundant (Bahula), the wind (Vayu), the whole (Sakala), the eye of all (Sarvalochana), the ground (Tala), the rhythm (Tala), holding a pot in his hand (Karasthali), of mighty frame (Urdhvasamhanana) and great (Mahan).

He is the umbrella (Chhatra), the good umbrella (Suchhatra), the famous (Vikhyata), the world (Loka), the shelter of all (Sarvashraya), the order (Krama), shaven (Munda), of odd form (Virupa), changed in form (Vikrita), bearing a staff (Dandi), a water pot (Kundi) and the one who takes many forms (Vikurvana).

He has lion's eyes (Haryaksha), is the directions (Kakubha), holds the thunderbolt (Vajri), has a hundred tongues (Shatajihva), a thousand feet (Sahasrapat), a thousand heads (Sahasramurdha); he is king of the gods (Devendra), made of all the gods (Sarvadevamaya) and the teacher (Guru).

He has a thousand arms (Sahasrabahu), is every limb (Sarvanga), the refuge (Sharanya), the maker of all worlds (Sarvalokakrit), the purifier (Pavitra), the mantra of the three peaks (Trikakunmantra), the youngest (Kanishtha) and dark and tawny (Krishnapingala).

He made the rod of Brahma (Brahmadandavinirmata), has the hundred-killer, the noose and the spear (Shataghnipashashaktiman), the lotus within (Padmagarbha), the great womb (Mahagarbha), the Veda within (Brahmagarbha) and is born from water (Jalodbhava).

He is the ray (Gabhasti), maker of the Veda (Brahmakrit), Brahman, knower of Brahman (Brahmavid), the Brahmin (Brahmana), the goal (Gati), of endless forms (Anantarupa), the one Self (Ekatma), of sharp brilliance (Tigmateja) and self-born (Svayambhuva).

His self rises upward (Urdhvagatma); he is lord of creatures (Pashupati), swift as the wind (Vataramha), swift as the mind (Manojava), wearing sandal (Chandani), the tip of the lotus stalk (Padmanalagra), the one who lifts the cow Surabhi (Surabhyuttarana) and the man (Nara).

He wears a great garland of karnikara flowers (Karnikaramahasragvi), has a blue crown (Nilamauli), holds the Pinaka bow (Pinakabhrit), is husband of Uma (Umapati), beloved of Uma (Umakanta), bearer of the Ganga (Jahnavibhrit) and lord of Uma (Umadhava).

He is the best (Vara), the boar (Varaha), the giver of boons (Varada), worthy to be chosen (Varenya), with a very great voice (Sumahasvana), very gracious (Mahaprasada), the tamer (Damana), slayer of enemies (Shatruha) and white and tawny (Shvetapingala).

He is of pleased nature (Pritatma), the Supreme Self (Paramatma), of controlled self (Prayatatma), the upholder of nature (Pradhanadhrit), the one who gives joy on all sides (Sarvaparshvasukha), three-eyed (Tryaksha), the common ground of dharma (Dharmasadharana) and the best (Vara).

He is the self of moving and unmoving things (Characharatma), the subtle self (Sukshmatma), immortal (Amrita), lord of the bull (Govrisheshvara), the Sadhyas and the sages (Sadhyarshi), the Vasu, the Aditya, Vivasvan, Savita and nectar (Amrita).

He is Vyasa, creation (Sarga), the short summary (Susankshepa) and the full account (Vistara), the cycle (Paryaya), the man (Nara), the season (Ritu), the year (Samvatsara), the month (Masa), the fortnight (Paksha) and the end of all counting (Sankhyasamapana).

He is the units of time, kala, kashtha, lava and matra, the hour, the day, the night and the moment; he is the field of the universe (Vishvakshetra), the seed of creatures (Prajabija), the linga (Linga), the first (Adya) and the good way out (Sunirgama).

He is what is and what is not (Sadasat), the manifest and the unmanifest (Vyaktam Avyaktam), father (Pita), mother (Mata) and grandfather (Pitamaha), the door to heaven, the door of birth and the door to liberation (Svargadvara, Prajadvara, Mokshadvara), and heaven itself (Trivishtapa).

He is final freedom (Nirvana), the one who gives delight (Hladana), the world of Brahma (Brahmaloka), the highest goal (Para Gati), the maker of gods and demons (Devasuravinirmata) and the final refuge of gods and demons (Devasuraparayana).

He is the teacher of gods and demons (Devasuraguru), the God (Deva), bowed to by gods and demons (Devasuranamaskrita), the great measure of gods and demons (Devasuramahamatra) and the shelter of the hosts of gods and demons (Devasuraganashraya).

He is overseer of the hosts of gods and demons (Devasuraganadhyaksha), their leader (Devasuraganagrani), the first God of the gods (Devadideva), the divine sage (Devarshi) and the giver of boons to gods and demons (Devasuravaraprada).

He is lord of gods and demons (Devasureshvara), the universe (Vishva), the great lord of gods and demons (Devasuramaheshvara), made of all gods (Sarvadevamaya), beyond thought (Achintya), the self of the gods (Devatatma) and born of himself (Atmasambhava).

He is the sprouting plant (Udbhit), the one of three strides (Trivikrama), the healer (Vaidya), stainless (Viraja), free of passion (Niraja), immortal (Amara), worthy of praise (Idya), lord of elephants (Hastishvara), the tiger (Vyaghra), the lion among gods (Devasimha) and the bull among men (Nararshabha).

He is the wise (Vibudha), the first and best (Agravara), subtle (Sukshma), all the gods (Sarvadeva), made of austerity (Tapomaya), well-joined (Suyukta), beautiful (Shobhana), holder of the thunderbolt (Vajri), source of spears (Prasanam Prabhava) and undying (Avyaya).

He is Guha, the lovely (Kanta), his own creation (Nija Sarga), the purifier (Pavitra), the purifier of all (Sarvapavana), horned (Shringi), fond of horns (Shringapriya), tawny (Babhru), king of kings (Rajaraja) and free of disease (Niramaya).

He is delightful (Abhirama), the host of gods (Suragana), the rest (Virama), the means of all (Sarvasadhana), with an eye on his forehead (Lalataksha), the god of all (Vishvadeva), the deer (Harina) and the splendour of holiness (Brahmavarchasa).

He is lord of unmoving things (Sthavaranam Pati), the one who strengthens discipline and the senses (Niyamendriyavardhana), with aims fulfilled (Siddhartha), whose purpose is accomplished (Siddhabhutartha), beyond thought (Achintya), true to his vows (Satyavrata) and pure (Shuchi).

He is lord of vows (Vratadhipa), the highest Brahman (Param Brahma), the one who shows grace to devotees (Bhaktanugrahakaraka), free (Vimukta), of released brilliance (Muktateja), glorious (Shriman), the increaser of fortune (Shrivardhana) and the world (Jagat).
So, with devotion, I have praised the Blessed Lord by his chief names, he whom neither Brahma and the other gods nor the sages truly know.

first: स्तोतव्यमर्च्यं वन्द्यं च कः स्तोष्यति जगत्पतिम् ।
en: Who could praise the lord of the world, who is to be praised, worshipped and bowed to? Yet, putting devotion first, I praised the all-pervading lord of sacrifice,
after receiving his permission, he who is the best of the wise. One who praises the God Shiva with these names, which increase well-being,
always devoted and made pure, reaches the Self through the self. This is the highest Brahman, and he reaches the highest Brahman.
The sages and gods, devoted to him, praise him with this hymn. When praised by self-controlled people, Mahadeva is pleased.
The Blessed Lord, all-pervading, is kind to devotees and makes them rest in the Self. In the same way, among human beings, the foremost people,
who believe and have faith, over many births, with hymns and with single-minded devotion, worship the Lord, the highest eternal God,
of boundless brilliance, by action, mind, speech and feeling. Lying down or awake, walking or sitting,
opening or closing their eyes, thinking of him again and again, hearing of Bhava, making others hear, and speaking of him,
praising him and being praised, they are happy and delighted. Through thousands of millions of births in many kinds of worldly life,
when a being's sins are gone, devotion to Bhava is born. Once born, this devotion to Bhava is single-minded and with one's whole being.
It is always the cause of complete freedom for such a person. Such unbroken, pure and steady devotion to Rudra is hard to gain even among gods, and is not commonly found among humans.
It is by his grace alone that devotion arises in people.
By it, those whose minds are fixed on him reach the highest perfection. Those who, with their whole being, take refuge in Maheshvara,
the God who loves those who surrender lifts them out of worldly life. Other gods do not free people from worldly life in this way.
For humans there is no other power or strength of austerity apart from this God. So, Krishna, the Blessed Lord, master of what is and what is not,
who wears a hide, was praised by Tandi, who was like Indra and of good mind. Brahma himself kept this hymn to the Lord.
It is sung, and one who sings it awakens in the presence of Brahma and Shankara. It is holy, purifying, and always destroys sin.

first: योगदं मोक्षदं चैव स्वर्गदं तोषदं तथा ।
en: It gives yoga, liberation, heaven and contentment. Those who recite it in this way with single devotion to Shankara

first: या गतिस्सांख्ययोगानां व्रजन्ते तां गतिं तथा ।
en: reach the same goal as the followers of Sankhya and Yoga. A devotee who practises this hymn carefully, always near Rudra,
for one year gains the fruit he desires. This is the highest secret, kept in the heart of Brahma.

first: ब्रह्मा प्रोवाच शक्राय शक्रः प्रोवाच मृत्यवे।
en: Brahma told it to Indra, Indra told it to Death, Death told it to the Rudras, and from the Rudras it came to Tandi.
Tandi gained it through great austerity in the home of Brahma. Tandi told it to Shukra, and Shukra, son of Bhrigu, told it to Gautama.
Madhava, Gautama told it to Manu, son of Vivasvan. Manu told it to the wise Narayana, the Sadhya, who was dear to him.
The Blessed Narayana, the Sadhya, the unfailing, told it to Yama. The Blessed Yama, son of Vivasvan, told it to Nachiketa.
Descendant of Vrishni, Nachiketa told it to Markandeya. Janardana, I received it from Markandeya with proper discipline.
Slayer of enemies, I will now give you this hymn, which is little known. It leads to heaven, gives health and long life, brings blessing, and is equal to the Veda.
Danavas, Yakshas and Rakshasas, Pishachas, Yatudhanas, Guhyakas and serpents cannot create any obstacle for one who recites it.

first: यः पठेत शुचिः पार्थ ब्रह्मचारी जितेन्द्रियः।
en: Son of Pritha, one who is pure, chaste and has controlled his senses, and who recites this for a year without breaking his practice, gains the merit of the horse sacrifice.
